extracted.intended_audience: Citizens of the State of New York (voters/delegates considering ratification of the U.S. Constitution)
extracted.subtask_description: Analytic political-constitutional essay assessing the strengths and weaknesses of confederate (federal) systems using historical examples to draw lessons for the proposed U.S. Constitution. Focuses on institutional design features that promote or undermine stability and effective government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocation of national vs. state powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Commerce, finance, negotiation, and war seem to comprehend all the objects which have charms for minds governed by that passion; and all the powers necessary to those objects ought, in the first instance, to be lodged in the national depository. The administration of private justice between the citizens of the same State, the supervision of agriculture and of other concerns of a similar nature, all those things... are proper to be provided for by local legislation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guides division of authority: centralize powers over external and general concerns (commerce, finance, diplomacy, war) while leaving domestic police, civil/criminal justice, and local economic regulation to states. Rationale: centralization of general powers is necessary for effectiveness; local matters are better managed locally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Likelihood of state encroachment vs. federal usurpation
rubrics_metrics.description: It will always be far more easy for the State governments to encroach upon the national authorities than for the national government to encroach upon the State authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluates directional risk of encroachment: because state governments are closer to the people and possess more direct influence, they are more likely to intrude on national authority. Institutional design should account for this asymmetry of influence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local administration of justice as source of popular attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: There is one transcendant advantage belonging to the province of the State governments... I mean the ordinary administration of criminal and civil justice. This, of all others, is the most powerful, most universal, and most attractive source of popular obedience and attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that courts and everyday legal administration create popular loyalty; leaving these to local governments produces strong local allegiance which shapes political dynamics and can counterbalance central power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visibility of national benefits and popular attachment
rubrics_metrics.description: The operations of the national government, on the other hand, falling less immediately under the observation of the mass of the citizens, the benefits derived from it will chiefly be perceived and attended to by speculative men.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Argues that national-level benefits are less tangible to ordinary citizens, producing weaker popular attachment to the union. Design should consider how to make federal benefits visible or rely on elites for broader support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical efficacy vs. paper powers (need for enforceable federal instruments)
rubrics_metrics.description: In theory, and upon paper, this apparatus of powers seems amply sufficient for all general purposes... Very different, nevertheless, was the experiment from the theory. The powers, like those of the present Congress, were administered by deputies appointed wholly by the cities... Hence the weakness, the disorders, and finally the destruction of the confederacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that enumerated powers are insufficient unless the federal structure has credible means to enforce them and prevent corruption/influence over deputies; institutional enforcement mechanisms are essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Danger of powerful members dominating the federation
rubrics_metrics.description: The more powerful members, instead of being kept in awe and subordination, tyrannized successively over all the rest. Athens... was the arbiter of Greece seventy-three years. The Lacedaemonians next governed it twenty-nine years...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A federation must guard against domination by the largest/powerful members; otherwise decision-making devolves into rule by the strongest, undermining equality and stability among members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unanimity requirements produce paralysis
rubrics_metrics.description: In all important cases, not only the provinces but the cities must be unanimous... In all these cases, however, unanimity and the sanction of their constituents are requisite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies unanimity rules (as in the United Netherlands) as a structural flaw that impedes timely decision-making and response, particularly in foreign policy and war.

rubrics_metrics.name: Necessary common attributes of effective union (treasury, troops, coin, judicatory)
rubrics_metrics.description: They have no common treasury; no common troops even in war; no common coin; no common judicatory; nor any other common mark of sovereignty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using the Swiss cantons as a negative example: absence of shared fiscal, military, monetary, and judicial institutions severely limits a union's capacity for collective action and defense; these are markers of effective sovereignty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delays and indecision in federal military preparedness
rubrics_metrics.description: Military preparations must be preceded by so many tedious discussions, arising from the jealousies, pride, separate views, and clashing pretensions of sovereign bodies, that before the diet can settle the arrangements, the enemy are in the field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Highlights that federative deliberative processes can be too slow for urgent military needs; an effective union requires quicker executive/military decision mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign exploitation of internal divisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Foreign nations have long considered themselves as interested in the changes made by events in this constitution; and have, on various occasions, betrayed their policy of perpetuating its anarchy and weakness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A weak, divided confederacy invites foreign interference and manipulation; protecting against external exploitation requires internal cohesion and unity of policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Uniformity of laws, measures, and money promotes moderation and justice
rubrics_metrics.description: It appears that the cities had all the same laws and customs, the same weights and measures, and the same money... The popular government... caused no disorders in the members of the Achaean republic, BECAUSE IT WAS THERE TEMPERED BY THE GENERAL AUTHORITY AND LAWS OF THE CONFEDERACY.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uniform legal and economic standards across members can temper faction and reduce disorder; suggests harmonization as a stabilizing design feature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Local governments' proximity to citizens creates diffuse influence
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a known fact in human nature, that its affections are commonly weak in proportion to the distance or diffusiveness of the object... the people of each State would be apt to feel a stronger bias towards their local governments than towards the government of the Union.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains emotional/political foundations for state-level loyalty; institutional design must reckon with local attachments that can compete with federal authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subdividing federative enforcement (e.g., circles) does not cure constitutional defects
rubrics_metrics.description: The experiment of dividing the empire into nine or ten circles or districts... has only served to demonstrate more fully the radical vice of the constitution. Each circle is the miniature picture of the deformities of this political monster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warns that creating intermediate administrative units or delegating enforcement to sub-units will not remedy fundamental constitutional weaknesses unless the core problem of sovereign fragmentation is addressed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Risk that federative alliances lead to anarchy among members rather than central tyranny
rubrics_metrics.description: It emphatically illustrates the tendency of federal bodies rather to anarchy among the members, than to tyranny in the head.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarizes central normative claim: confederacies without sufficient central authority are more prone to internecine disorder than to oppressive central rule; design trade-offs must be acknowledged.
